name: Linux TCP splice transparent acceleration
summary: Experimental opt-in forwarded IPv4 TCP split on Linux TUN egress with native splice and selectable client-facing kernel CC; not a generic acceleration claim.

usage.cli: wbd-v4-server --tcp-proxy-cc bbr --tcp-proxy-port 46180 (omit cc for original NAT)

verification.scope: H2423 prior source finite duplex/half-close/UDP and Stop, H2429 listener/lifecycle candidate not yet measured
H2423 prior source finite duplex/half-close/UDP and Stop, H2429 listener/lifecycle candidate not yet measured

limitations: IPv4 forwarded TCP only; local server services and UDP unchanged
End-to-end TCP acknowledgement becomes two real TCP segments
No custom CC algorithm implemented; old-kernel and physical paths not verified
H2417 did forward real TCP, but 21Mbps DERP-limited path and incomplete matrix preclude performance qualification; see docs/evidence/M0/20261125-H2417-LINUX-TCP-SPLICE-FIRST.json
H2426 matched FEC 30% default fq_codel splice -11% both orders; no general performance gain. H2427 fixed fq maxrate is a separate bottleneck. H2429 correctness candidate unqualified.
